conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you in any way.

Today I’ll be using a short questionnaire called the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. It’s simply a 10-question snapshot of how things have been going for you over the past seven days. We use it with every new parent because the early weeks can bring big emotions that are hard to sort out on your own.

Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me something that makes me worry about your immediate safety, and then we’ll talk together about the best next steps. Feel free to answer honestly; there are no right or wrong responses, and many new moms find it a relief to put words to what they’re experiencing.

We’ll go through one question at a time. Ready to begin?

Over the past week, have you still been able to look forward with enjoyment to things, or has that feeling been harder to come by?

Honestly, it’s been… harder. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but now it feels kind of flat. I can still enjoy a few things for a minute, like when the baby smiles, but the feeling fades fast, and I’m back to this heavy “what’s-the-point” mood.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes I can laugh, but it’s like I have to force it or it just slips away right after. My sister sent a goofy meme yesterday and I chuckled for a second, then felt guilty because I thought, “Why can’t I just feel light like I used to?” Most of the time the funny side feels pretty far away.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I mean, I’ll think, “Maybe I’ll feel better if I meet a friend for coffee,” but when the time comes, it just feels like another chore. Even little things I used to love—like watching a favorite show—don’t give me that spark anymore.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that a lot. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it must be something I did—like I ate the wrong thing, or I’m not soothing him the “right” way. Last night he wouldn’t settle and I just kept thinking, “Other moms figure this out, why can’t I?” I know, rationally, babies just cry, but the guilt still jumps on me.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s too quiet—so I poke him to make sure he’s breathing. Then I worry I woke him for no reason. It’s like my mind hops from one “what-if” to the next, even when nothing’s actually happening.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes. It’s happened three or four times this week. Out of nowhere my chest gets tight, I feel shaky, and I’m convinced something awful is about to happen—even if I’m just sitting on the couch. It passes after a few minutes, but in that moment I feel like I need to run or hide, except I don’t even know what I’m running from.
Things have been getting on top of me

A lot of days, yeah. It’s like the second I open my eyes there’s this pile of stuff—laundry, bottles, texts I haven’t answered—and it feels so heavy I don’t know where to start. I usually push through because the baby needs me, but I’m running on empty and snapping at little things, then feeling worse for snapping.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning with all the “what-ifs” about the baby, and I can’t shut it off. Most nights this week I stared at the ceiling for over an hour, then woke up two or three times with anxious thoughts racing again. Even when the baby’s asleep, I’m not really resting.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most days I do. It’s like this gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll be changing the baby’s diaper and suddenly feel like I could cry for no real reason. I’m not weepy every single minute, but the sadness creeps in several times a day and it’s hard to shake.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened twice this week. Once was yesterday when the baby wouldn’t nap and I just sat in the rocker with tears running down while he finally slept on my chest. I felt so alone and useless, even though I knew he was fine.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

A couple of times, very briefly. I’ve had that fleeting “what if I just wasn’t here” thought when everything feels too heavy, but I haven’t made any plans and I don’t want to leave my baby. It scares me that the idea even pops in, so I push it away fast.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother (baby approx. ≤12 wks)  
Date: ___  
Screener: Lic. MH Professional  

A. Positive findings (patient endorses ≥1 option 0–3 unless noted)  
- Anhedonia: diminished laughter, anticipatory pleasure ↓ (Q1, Q2)  
- Low mood: persistent sadness, “gray cloud,” frequent tearfulness (Q8, Q9)  
- Guilt / self-blame: automatic, irrational responsibility for infant distress (Q3)  
- Anxiety: daily free-floating worry, somatic tension, nocturnal rumination (Q4)  
- Panic: 3–4 discrete episodes/week, chest tightness, urge to flee (Q5)  
- Overwhelm / impaired coping: tasks feel “heavy,” irritability (Q6)  
- Sleep disturbance: initial & middle insomnia linked to anxious cognitions (Q7)  

B. Safety  
- Passive SI: fleeting “what if I wasn’t here” thoughts this week, no plan or intent (Q10) → elevated risk, requires formal risk assessment.  

C. Pattern summary  
Profile consistent with moderate–severe postpartum depressive symptoms with comorbid anxiety; functional impact evident (self-care, infant care, social withdrawal).  

D. Screening conclusion  
Meets threshold for immediate referral to OB/GYN or psychiatric provider for comprehensive evaluation, possible diagnosis, and safety planning. Continue supportive monitoring; provide crisis resources now.
